reviews.text: Game of the Year so far
First Review! Cute graphics, fun gameplay. so far so good. No bugs after finishing one island quality work.

I think this is a quaint, well structured strategy game. The art style immediately stands out for how cute and polished it is, which gives the game an attractive element regardless of its gameplay. The combat is relatively typical for the genre of tile based tactical games, but its dice rolling gimmick adds some novelty to the experience. Even in the early game status effects and usable items feel relatively meaningful, and especially come in handy when fighting the first boss, which gives the system more depth over outright damage racing. The skill trees are surprisingly expansive, and players will acquire a steady supply of items and gear to further customize their party. This gives the player a small break in between fights as they build up their characters, and offers them a good amount of variety for the combat. Based on what can be seen the game appears to have a decent amount of content, especially as there are multiple difficulty levels above average that incentive future runs; although I do not imagine the game is too expansive overall currently. To me the adorable art style and decent combat variety really helps give the game a solid appeal beyond other, typical games of this genre. The system feels well designed and is fun to engage with, while looking good in the process. If you're interested in finding more games like this I've probably reviewed quite a few on my curator page [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/38950844-Anoemalous/] here [/url].

TLDR: 8.5 cute xcom style game with a decent but cast of characters with their own (somewhat restrictive) play styles and awesome item variety. Skills are also not locked into place letting you completely change the game between every battle if you so choose. Played this immediately upon release as I was waiting quite impatiently for it to come out so my words will be a bit biased. That being said I love me an xcom style game and this one delivers well. Been a long time since I’ve reviewed a game so I’ll just do some pros and cons after finishing my first game on the 2nd hardest difficulty on my first attempt. Pros: Art style. Nuff said difficulty style (more complex rather that straight dmg/health increases from enemies) skills and item variety, undo move button, elements mean something: you can make someone wet to counteract fire enemies and also give yourself extra lightning damage Adjustable final boss: you can fight the boss after completing 2, 3 or 4 islands leading to it being more difficult with each completion. Nice if you’re playing a bad team comp but still want to beat the boss. Bosses: each boss has their own elements and playable similar to their minions you’ve encountered on the island Item variety : honestly it has so many items to do I think every status effect or action in the game in some way and allow you to push a character to account for weaknesses or go full ham into their strengths. I love em so much it makes me think they should’ve put more into the skills rather than the items but preferences as there are multiple characters who can use (almost) any item. Cons: no undo action: for keyboard it’s not as important but on controller scheme it’s very easy to accidentally attack the wrong area and end up killing yourself in an aoe Synergies (while some exist for the most part each character has their own thing and doesn’t play well with more than one other character meaning you might have two guys multiplying their damage output out the wazoo while the other one kinda sits there away from them so as not to mess up the elemental matchups relatability (I can’t say for certain since I haven’t gotten there but I estimate I’ll be able to get maybe 5 more unique runs out of this (8 characters/teams of 3) before I’ve done everything I can. I like achievement hunting so 60% complete after my first run is a bit disheartening Bosses: I think the bosses are for the most part way to easy, even with their immunities with the occasional crazy one shot capability. Yeah they have more actions and health than normal enemies but even when I chose not to read their skills before engaging I found that I could still easily beat them. That being said I’m just an overly negative sounding person. Absolutely love the concept and style of this and don’t regret the $18 I spent on it at all. If you like xcom style games and eat something cute yet still complex in a good amount of areas I recommend it. 8.5/10

This is by no means a bad game, but you constantly feel that the developers don't have much experience in this genre. Everything that's already in the game works well, and the amusing visual style doesn't detract from that at all. However, the game systems lack depth. In terms of mechanics, each character has a rigid archetype that the game does not allow to be shifted in any direction. The enemies, although they look funny, are also quite monotonous. I can't tell you how the basic fish enemy differs from the basic pig enemy: all they do is run towards you and try to hit or shoot you. The locations, although they look different, don't contain any additional mechanics to diversify the gameplay in any way. On the first island, there were still some attempts to make interesting missions, where you had to collect chickens and escort a cart. But on the second island, everything became much more monotonous. In general, this game is essentially in early access, even though it's not stated anywhere. I really hope that the developers will be able to earn enough money to add the much-needed content here!

Definitely a bit undercooked, but not bad for a two person team. The aesthetic is great. The mechanics are solid. The execution is lacking. The enemy/level design feels too shallow for this to be a rougelike, I did every island and I was already quite weary by the middle of the 3rd island. I do not intend to do another run. The levels and enemies are just not very exciting. I played on the second highest difficulty, perhaps the highest difficulty makes enemies more interesting (it says something about an advanced moveset I think). Most of the time after the first island enemies were just not challenging at all. I only had one death, on the final boss. There was one close call on another boss, and that was it. The items are fun, if not so balanced. The ones which add new actions are definitely my favorite, which is a shame since they aren't the strongest of them usually. Bonus challenges, which give an extra reward when completed in each combat, are either easy or tedious, and which ones can appear are based on what you can complete (you won't be asked to kill enemies with ranged attacks if you have no ranged attacks). This lead me to avoid picking up certain skills to narrow the pool, even if I wanted the skill. Having only one ability which does a certain damage type, applies a certain buff, or is melee/ranged is a pain because you will get a challenge which will necessitate stalling to complete sometimes. Another min-maxxy complaint I have is with the ranger, who can get a skill which gives extra gold when killing enemies. This means you want to funnel as many kills into the ranger as possible (and presumably take it in every run, as it just gives you more resources). Hopefully some of the blatant issues (didn't list any here) and common feedback will get some changes made to the game before too long. It's not a bad start, they really did nail some of it.

Despite there being a great framework for a genuinely fun game here, the game as it stands is too shallow and still feels like early access. 3 character party is too limiting. Enemies and different islands don't feel unique enough. Player units don't feel like you can really build them in a unique way from anyone else, there needs to be more skills for each tier and perhaps 1 or 2 more skill tiers overall. A lot of the skills that players get to choose from have modifiers that feel like bloat or like they already should have been included in the base ability. +1 damage on abilities is boring, I would like to see more interesting effects that trigger on kill or maybe have positional requirements. Too few player classes to choose from. No meta progression outside of unlocking new characters. Game is too easy and lacks modifiers to make runs feel unique or challenging. This game also would be great for multiplayer if the above issues were fixed, but I won't hold that against it.

The game and mechanics behind the game are "fine". It's a good idea but badly needs some things to improve on replayability. I beat 2 islands and was told I could go fight the final boss early. I thought sure i'll try that. I beat it and then that's it. I didnt unlock anything, no upgrades, no new start. I had to completely start over and basically play the same characters, with the same general missions, and nothing really new. Right now the only reason to play is to unlock a few more characters. It's like the game wants to be a roguelike but forgot to add in progression. Every achievement could be start with x gold or every 10 achievements start with 1 skill point. It at least allows some variety. Skill tress are also very static for now, but that I can live with. I just dont have a desire to keep grinding knowing that there isnt much to gain from beating the game repeatedly. This game has great potential and I do hope they add some adjustments to starting the game or modifiers or something.

The demo and first couple levels leaves a great impression: a great art style evokes childhood nostalgia of playing with action figures (or dolls), the dice-rolling mechanic feels satisfying, and the gameplay feels quite solid. But after those first ~2 hours, you realize that the gameplay feels solid is because it's retreading old ground. It's the same basic tactics game that we've all played before, solving nothing new and often not even implementing 'solved' gameplay design problems. For example, the skill tree has a lot of nodes that are just +1 damage. Sigh. Really? Or, on later islands, you'll often load into a battle and see that it STARTS with like 20 enemies and then has another three spawning tents, which is just wearying to see. On the highest difficulty, there's some challenge, but at anything below, it's just grind. Or, on the highest tactician difficulty, you'll sometimes get completely boned because enemies spawn in and 100%->0% your defense objective without any counterplay options available to you. Or that there is no real narrative, no real character arcs. I don't know why indie games keep trying to make these roguelikes when it's almost impossible for an indie dev to make enough content or variety to sustain that many replays. That's certainly the case here, which has zero meta progression, except for unlocking ~5 new heroes. In summary, I beat it twice, with a 4 island run on second highest difficulty, then a 2 island run on highest difficulty w/ three different heroes. And I'm good. Which, if this has been $10, I'd be pretty satisfied. I actually PREFER short games. But at $20? That's steep, too steep. If you really dig the art style and are looking for something short and simple but satisfying, I think this is a very solid $10 game, though there's better out there. At $20, though, nah.

Disclaimer: I like this game a lot but I wouldn't recommend it at it's current state for the following reasons: 1. This isn't a roguelike. Calling it one isn't even a stretch, it is a lie. It is a cozy strategy RPG - absolutely nothing wrong with that! - and randomization is so barely present and when it is present it does not make a difference because... 2. This game does not even remotely have enough content to justify the existence of its FOUR locations. Enemies across different locations behave exactly the same, have the same abilities and the biggest differences between them is their health bar and how much damage they deal. What I said about enemies is true of all missions as well. There are a handful and the game won't stop repeating them across all locations. Items are mostly meaningless. There are some items that encourage actually trying out different builds but most items are really not that deep and the bonuses they offer are either not worth considering at all or have the worth of exactly one skill point - this means shops and farming for items becomes irrelevant compared to farming skill points. Loot that is actually interesting is so scarce that you never worry about what equipment piece goes to which party member. The fact that there's so little actual content while requirering you to do that many missions... 3. leads to a game with severe pacing issues. Missions start to feel like a chore. Rewards stay static from beginning to end. Imagine playing Slay The Spire and after every battle you choose between the same 3 cards. I like the game. It has a charming presentation, what is there is polished, no bugs, clean UI and save system but what there is is just not enough. I hope the Devs will add A LOT more content to the game or restructure it as a much shorter experience because otherwise this game isn't worth your money or time after the first 2-4 hours and removing the roguelike tag would be nice because it very clearly isn't one and doesn't even try to be one. Feels like the devs weren't confident enough for commiting to the cozy dice strategy game but embracing this side of the game would have been the better choice. edit: I think I came across a little too harsh so I clarified some things.

Dobbel is great fun even for hardcore TBS lovers, just dont expect much. Its also a good starter game for people unfamiliar with this genre. Am looking forward to maybe a sci-fi ground or space game from this company, or cruising the high seas, or cleaning up the streets in 20th century Crime City or whatever.

What an incredible little strategy game this is. I've played a lot of games in this genre and this one was obviously made with a ton of love. The two main selling points for me are the well thought out mechanics and gameplay + the incredible claymation like graphics. It all blends together very well. Perfect for when you just want to roll some dice and relax with a few strategic battles. If I had to complain about something it would be the very simplistic story and the lack of progression in between fully new runs. I also would have loved even more complexity in the skill trees and character progression + itemization but it still does a very good job at keeping me entertained. If you aren't sure then I strongly recommend you try the very generous demo, the charm and heart in this is likely to win you over.

This is a really nice game with loads of depth in the strategy, even tho its rather simple and intuitive. Higher dificulty does give a challenge, and this game indeed plays like a roguelite once you start doing multiple runs and unlocking all characters. The dice system is rather refreshing for the genre, and puts an interestng resource management into combat, instead of mana, action points or raw statistics. This game has nice cute and simple aesthetic, good graphics for its proposal. As for improvements, I wish this game got some expansions eventually, with more content and characters, game modes and enemies.

I was REALLY excited to play this game after playing the demo, and it feels like a game that has all the right ingredients for one of the best narrative tactical RPGs i've played in years, but unfortunately it was all thrown into a subpar roguelike instead. The game really feels like it was just not built to be a roguelike, but was forced into one. The characters are all well designed and have clearly defined roles, but all that charm you see from the opening tutorial goes to waste because you never see any more dialogue from them ever again. I was excited to see their growth and the plot of the game from the beginning, but it just isn't there. The characters all have innate skill trees which would have worked great in a regular campaign, but in a roguelike it means you pretty much always choose the same characters and the same skills for each character every run, removing all the variation you'd want in a roguelike. ALL of the maps are perfectly flat rectangular maps with little variation, only differing minimally based on the mission type, so it just becomes SUPER repetitive and bland. i assume this is to allow for some form of randomized layout, but all that's being randomized is the trees in my way. Hand-crafted levels would have carried this game for miles, but the maps we get just feel so disappointing. The equipment you can get from the shops are basically all completely useless aside from the ones that give you extra dice and movement range, which is basically a staple of the tactical genre, but it just means there's really no reason to use 90% of the other items unless you happen to get SUPER lucky and get a crazy item from one of the shops, because they don't restock for the entire run, which they should. The optional objectives pigeonhole you into ignoring certain skills and equipment, because god forbid i find an item that gives me a skill my party shouldn't have. because now that skill is in the pool for the optional tasks and I'll have a task that's way harder than the other because only the person with that item can even attempt it. it incentivizes you to deliberately not upgrade certain skills, because now they can stun or something, and then I have the same problem of only one person having the capability of doing the optional task. Because this is a turn-based tactical style game, the stages themselves are NOT quick, so runs last well over an hour or two. This basically makes you so exhausted with the recycled maps and enemies by the end that you have NO desire to actually do another run. I want to say I REALLY wanted this game to be good, because it just had so much potential, but unfortunately it was all wasted.

The art for the game is fantastic, but the core gameplay is subpar. The difficulty felt properly tuned at the start of a run, but my characters strength rapidly outgrew the difficulty. I did not have to strategize outside of the first 20% of the run.

To be honest, this seems like a title almost begging to be ported to the Switch. Peak bite-sized gaming with broad appeal. Give it a go. Honestly, the price is right.
